rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Game End Overview Play cards to the table to attempt to control all outposts by gaining control and switching them to your color. Turn Play 1 card to your side of an Outpost If the outpost is currently of opposite colour & the total strength of your cards is greater than your opponent's take control of the outpost If you take control of an outpost, apply the outposts effect Round End If a player controls all outposts simultaneously, they win immediately If a player plays their last card without triggering the end of the round, one outpost is selected that cannot be flipped and their opponent takes one additional turn. The player with the most outputs then wins Game End First player to win 2 rounds wins the game

[Rating: 5/10] On the surface it sounds like yet another Battle Line clone, however Drones vs. Seagulls carves out a solid niche in a stagnating genre. Here the real trick is to perform intricate combos. Whenever you switch control, you trigger a special power which can trigger another control elsewhere. The goal is to establish simultaneous control of every area. Quite thinky and pretty enjoyable. My only beef with the game is that the design is too slim and many of the powers can easily be reduced into heuristics as to which you should try to control. I'd still play it again. The idea is a good one

[Rating: 6/10] Based on one play: Another one of those tug of war games where you place cards on one side of the board in order to control a column. In this one, there are 7 tokens in the middle, and you want them all to be flipped to your side. They flip when you gain control of the column by having a larger value on your side and that also gives you a bonus ability that triggers right away. You need to find a combo that lets you win or at least flip a few tokens at once. This mechanic has been done in so many games, and I did not find this one to stand out.
